chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: Hawkins and bebop; California audiences; Billy Berg's
summary: Hawkins supported the new music while Californians like Kid Ory disliked it; Hawkins' band plays eight weeks at Billy Berg's.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Because Hawk had a big influence on Jazz. Well, that's no more than right, though, because he was something, man. He was one of the first guys to latch onto it and to help promote it, you know, really. I always did admire him for that, because he wanted to play. I mean, like, he wanted to be in on everything that was new. He was in on it, and he wanted to be in on it.

And there were a lot of guys out there that really didn't like it, especially in California. People used to come by to hear Hawk, and they heard the band he had, and they'd tell me, 'Ah, why don't he play like he used to play?' and 'This ain't his thing.' Like, Kid Ory comes by and he said, 'Oh, man. This ain't the type of music I want to hear.' But I mean, we fixed him later on. He found out he couldn't hear it anyway, heh-heh. But I mean, he meant well. He just was into one type of thing, you know.

Dave Dexter had been talking to him and told him that he didn't dig what Hawk was doing either. But he was glad to give Hawk a date and get him in the studio. But he didn't like the way that the setup was for the band that we had in Billy Berg's.
So you went into Billy Berg's.
Yeah. We stayed there for eight weeks, at Billy Berg's...

Sir Charles, Oscar Pettiford, Denzil Best, me and Hawk. And Hawk and I, at that time, we had gotten pretty tight together, because I learned a lot of the things that he was doing and he learned some of the things that I was doing. So we had a very mutual agreement as far as playing was concerned, except for... The only thing our difference was, was money.
Well, we'll get to that record date. I remember you telling me about that.
